title: Sandboxed file and bash tools for mini-dsh
brief: Give mini-dsh the tools it needs to do real work, and a fence around them. Write read, write and edit tools that store a version for each file a session reads and refuse stale or unread edits. Write a bash tool that starts bash -c in the workspace with an environment cleaned of secrets and DSH_ names, a timeout and an output cap, and that reports a non-zero exit as information, not as an error. Then add sandbox modes: resolve each call's policy from the session's last sandbox/mode event, fence file writes with realpath and the write roots, and wrap every confined command in sandbox-exec on macOS or bwrap on Linux, refusing with SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE when neither works. Add the one-call escalation with sandbox_permissions and justification through the ApprovalService from the tool pipeline project, and a /permission command with two presets. Write in your README what the sandbox does not stop: reading any file your user can read, and the network. dsh's SAFETY.md says the same about its own sandbox, which has not been audited.

starter.note: New. read, write and edit built with defineTool; a per-session version map; exactly-once old_string; mayWrite before every change.
New. cleanEnv (drops /KEY|PASSWORD|SECRET|TOKEN/i and DSH_*) and run(program, args, options) with cwd, env, timeoutMs, maxBytes and signal.
New. The bash tool: exit code and output as its value, [exit code: N] in the rendered text, the sandbox denial line when the runner's text appears.
New. SandboxMode, writeRoots, mayWrite, resolvePolicy, confine (Seatbelt profile or bwrap arguments) and approveEscalation.
New. The preset table, currentPreset with custom, setPreset, and a /permission command.
New. Tests in a temporary workspace; confine tests check the argument list, and a live test runs only where sandbox-exec or bwrap exists.

hints: Compute a file's version from stat as mtimeMs and size, and store it under sessionId and path. Store the new version after every successful write or edit, or the second edit in a row fails.
Build the child environment from cleanEnv first and add NO_COLOR, TERM=dumb and PAGER=cat after it. Test it by running bash -c env with DEEPSEEK_API_KEY set in the parent and checking it is absent.
In mayWrite, call realpath on the target's folder, not on the target, because a file you are about to create does not exist yet. On macOS remember that /tmp is really /private/tmp.
Test confine by comparing argument lists, not by running them; then add one live test per platform that writes outside the roots and checks for Operation not permitted or Read-only file system.

In approveEscalation, check that the mode is strictly wider before you ask anyone, and pass the approved mode only into this call's policy. A test runs a second call without sandbox_permissions and checks it is confined again.

rubric.criterion: read stores a version per session and path; edit and write refuse an unread or changed file, and old_string must appear exactly once
bash runs in the workspace with secrets and DSH_ names removed, applies a 120000 ms default and 600000 ms cap and a 64000-byte cap, and reports a non-zero exit in a normal result

Each call's policy comes from the session's last sandbox/mode event or the default, write roots follow the three modes, realpath stops link escapes, and the README states that reads and the network are not confined

Confined commands run under sandbox-exec or bwrap with profiles that deny writes outside the roots, denials are reported to the model, and no usable runner gives SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE instead of an unconfined run
A denied call can be retried with sandbox_permissions and justification; only a strictly wider mode is asked about, allowed-once widens that call only, and a no is final
/permission switches between two presets by writing permission/preset and only the changed setting events, and settings that match no preset report custom

milestones.title: File tools with versions
milestones.body: Write read, write and edit. In a temporary workspace, read app.ts, change it from the test, and check that the model's edit is refused and succeeds after a second read.

milestones.title: A bash tool with a clean environment
milestones.body: Write cleanEnv, run and the bash tool. Check that env output lacks DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, that sleep 5 with timeoutMs 1000 stops after about 1 s, and that exit 1 gives a normal result ending in [exit code: 1].

milestones.title: Modes and write roots
milestones.body: Add SandboxMode, writeRoots, mayWrite and resolvePolicy, and fence the file tools. Under workspace-write a write to the workspace passes, a write to a link that points outside fails, and under read-only every write fails.

milestones.title: Confined commands
milestones.body: Add confine and use it in the bash tool for read-only and workspace-write. echo hi > ~/outside.txt must be denied with the sandbox denial line, and a host without a runner must give SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE.

milestones.title: Escalation and presets
milestones.body: Add approveEscalation and /permission. An approved retry to danger-full-access runs once and the next call is confined again; /permission danger-full-access writes 3 events, and a second identical switch writes none.
